title: Train and deploy SLO alert classifier to curb false burn pagers
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Multiple capacity/regression incidents over the past quarter produced high-volume burn-rate SLO alerts that were noisy and frequently false-positive (e.g., transient backend hiccups, autoscaler flapping, synthetic traffic anomalies). This ticket is the engineering plan to build, validate, and deploy a lightweight supervised classifier that ingests alert signals (burn rate, error spike shape, correlated tracing spans, recent rollout markers, autoscaler events, and historical noise fingerprints) to suppress or de-prioritize pagering of alerts that are likely noise while preserving high recall for true customer-impacting SLO breaches.

Goal: Reduce actionable pages from noise by at least 45% without losing more than 1% absolute recall on incidents that caused customer-facing errors in the last 12 months. The classifier will sit as a pre-pager filter in the burn-rate alert pipeline and emit reasons/tags for observability and auditability.
success_criteria: 1) Pager volume reduction: >=45% decrease in nightly and weekend pages attributable to burn-rate alerts (baseline: Jan-Feb 2026). 2) Incident recall: <=1% absolute drop in recall for historically labeled customer-impact incidents. 3) Explainability: each suppressed alert must include a short reason tag and a linkable evidence bundle to support post-incident review. 4) Ops acceptance: runbook updated and on-call training completed before full rollout.
implementation_plan: Data labeling sprint (2 weeks): sample ~3k burn alerts from last 12 months, label as 'noise'|'real' with on-call and SRE review — owners: Marcus + SRE rotation.

Feature prototype (1 week): extract features from existing alert payloads (time-series shape, percentile deltas, correlated 5xx traces, autoscaler events, deploy markers) and build tabular dataset stored in alerts-data-bucket.

Model training & validation (1 week): train a lightweight tree-based model (XGBoost/LightGBM) with cross-val on stratified folds; tune for high recall; produce precision/recall curves and confusion matrix.
Simulated dry-run (2 weeks): run classifier in 'audit' mode on production stream for 2 weeks; produce dashboards for false-suppression candidates; run human-in-the-loop review for borderline cases.

Safety gates & instrumentation (1 week): add fallback thresholds, minimum tokenized evidence, decision logging to event-store, and a manual override flag for on-call to re-enable paging for specific alerts.
Canary rollout (1 week): route 10% of burn alerts through the suppression path with human pager backup; monitor missed-incident KPI and escalate if recall drops beyond threshold.
Full rollout & postmortem (ongoing): ramp to 100%, schedule 30/60/90-day reviews and update runbooks and playbooks.
Automation & ownership: create CI job to retrain monthly and a GitHub PR template for model changes that requires SRE and PM signoff.
Documentation: Confluence doc, runbook updates, on-call notes, and a training session with SRE/Support.
Post-deploy eval: produce a 30-day impact report with pager reduction metrics and any missed incidents annotated.
notes: Prefer a simple, interpretable model initially to aid trust with SREs; avoid deep-learning blackbox for the first iteration. Keep model inline with alerting pipeline latency requirements (<50ms decision time) and ensure decision logs are retained for 90 days. Collaborate with SDX team for access to trace correlation APIs and with Platform for deployment in the alerting path.
